question: Should opaque outbound `channelData` be treated as user-visible egress and removed in full whenever any nested key or value contains protected internal runtime context?
rationale: Tests can prove the selected behavior, but they cannot decide the intended security-versus-payload-preservation policy for arbitrary channel-native data.

options.title: Approve whole-payload suppression
options.body: Treat every nested channelData key and value as outbound egress and discard the field on any protected-context match, prioritizing non-leakage over partial payload preservation.

options.title: Narrow the filtering contract
options.body: Require a maintainer-defined allowlist or narrower traversal rule before merge so legitimate opaque provider payloads are less likely to be discarded.

options.title: Keep parsing only
options.body: Remove the new channelData sanitizer and land only string-to-object normalization, accepting that opaque channelData remains outside this internal-context defense.

recommendation.title: Approve whole-payload suppression
recommendation.body: Treat every nested channelData key and value as outbound egress and discard the field on any protected-context match, prioritizing non-leakage over partial payload preservation.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history connects this owner to both internal-source message routing and channelData-based structured delivery, making them the strongest available reviewer for the boundary choice.
